Diagrammo (dgmo) — codebase report

Built 2026-11-19 at commit bfdb3d94

dgmo is the TypeScript library behind the Diagrammo diagram language: it parses text in the DGMO markup into SVG for dozens of chart types. The same repository also builds the dgmo command line tool (cli/) and a set of browser drop-in scripts (standalone/), and at this commit the library and the drop-ins are at version 0.100.0 and the CLI at 0.102.0. The measured source is 1,799 files and 409,501 lines, with the history running from 2026-02-07 to 2026-11-19 across 2,956 non-merge commits that change a file. A newcomer starts at src/index.ts (the public API), then src/render.ts (the render pipeline), then one chart folder such as src/sequence/. This report draws no data-model chart, no sitemap, no state chart and no journey map: the repo has no schema or database, no site, no status lifecycle and no user-facing app flow.

The stack

The repo publishes three packages: the library, the dgmo command line tool, which bundles the library and calls its render entry directly, and standalone browser scripts. Inside the library, one render entry parses the text, looks up the chart type, and hands the work to either the data-chart engine or a per-chart export handler. A newcomer should read src/render.ts first, because every path from a host app or the CLI goes through it. The outside services are the online editor (share links), the Diagrammo Cloud API (dgmo put/get/ls) and the MCP server (dgmo mcp).

Size by directory

Each box is a directory, sized by its lines of code, with 409,501 lines in total. 1799 files rolled up to 1217 boxes, two directory levels deep; gallery/fixtures, gallery/snapshots, src, src/utils, tests, tests/fixtures/completion-conformance, tests/fixtures/conformance, tests/fixtures/highlight-conformance hold more than 40 files of their own, shown as files. The smallest 1178 are shown as "(other)". The "(other)" box holds 211,302 lines (52% of the total) in 1,401 files, so the roll-up hid where most of the code sits: the directories the note above lists as holding more than the file limit (tests, gallery fixtures and snapshots, src and src/utils) are split into single files, and nearly all of those files fell into "(other)". Of what is named, src/ with one folder per chart type is the largest part; src/map is the biggest chart, and api-baseline is a checked-in snapshot of the built type files, not hand-written code.

Render a file with the CLI

When you run dgmo diagram.dgmo, the CLI reads the file, checks it with the parser, calls the library render function, and turns the SVG into a PNG with resvg. If the parser reports an error, the CLI replaces the SVG with an error card instead of a half drawn chart. The CLI itself holds only the file, flag and PNG handling; all drawing lives in the library.

Render from the library

This is the call a host app makes. render() picks the palette, parses the text, asks the parse router (dgmo-router.ts) for the chart category, and installs a temporary jsdom window because the renderers draw with D3. Data charts go to one engine; every other chart type goes through renderForExport and its table of per-chart handlers. If any diagnostic has error severity, the public wrapper in index.ts returns an error card by default.

Make a share link

dgmo share compresses the diagram text with lz-string and puts it in an online editor URL, so no server stores it. A diagram whose compressed text is over 8192 bytes is refused, and the command exits with an error. The result is printed and copied to the clipboard unless --no-copy is given.

How dgmo finds the chart type

A diagram names its type in the first word of the first line. When it does not, parseDgmoChartType checks for a live link, then tries a fixed list of ten looks-like tests in order, and the order matters: sequence is tested before flowchart because both use arrows. Only those ten types have a looks-like test; every other type must be named on the first line.

Library release

release.sh builds and checks locally, tags the version and starts the GitHub Actions release workflow. The workflow checks the tag against package.json, runs typecheck, lint, test and build, then publishes the library and the standalone package to npm with provenance. The script ends by asking npm which version it serves. The CLI has its own workflow (release-cli.yml) and tag.

Module dependencies

Each arc is a link from one directory to another; a thicker arc means more imports. 5060 file imports rolled up to 376 links between 69 directories, up to 2 levels deep, and the 30 least connected are shown as "(other)". Files that change together

Each arc joins two files that were changed in the same commit, with a thicker arc for more commits. Only the 30 most frequent of 42171 file pairs are shown, and 34 bulk commits touching more than 50 files were skipped. The top pair is src/map/layout.ts and tests/map-layout.test.ts (66 commits). The AI editor rules files (.cursorrules, .windsurfrules, the Copilot instructions, SKILL.md) share a block generated from docs/language-reference.md by scripts/gen-ai-core.mjs, so they often change in the same commit.
